q: In Premiere I'd create proxies on ingest. How does Revolution do it?
a: A Revolution proxy is a smaller, easier-to-decode copy shown while you edit; the export always reads the originals. Revolution makes them by itself in the background for clips that need them (4:2:2 H.265 / H.264, and 4K+ long-GOP while the setting is on); Clip ▸ Proxy ▸ Create Proxies… still makes them by hand.

q: What does the amber 4:2:2 badge mean?
a: An amber 4:2:2 badge marks a 4:2:2 H.265 clip with no proxy yet: the video engine can't decode it, so it's decoded in software (slow at 6.2K) and a proxy is recommended; such clips always get one. Proxy names carry a 16-character fingerprint of the original, so importing the same file again or opening it in another project reuses the proxy.

q: Does importing the same file in another project make a new proxy?
a: An amber 4:2:2 badge marks a 4:2:2 H.265 clip with no proxy yet: the video engine can't decode it, so it's decoded in software (slow at 6.2K) and a proxy is recommended; such clips always get one. Proxy names carry a 16-character fingerprint of the original, so importing the same file again or opening it in another project reuses the proxy.

q: When does the proxy worker run?
a: It steps aside whenever you work: while you play, scrub or export it finishes the frames in hand and waits, then starts again half a second after you stop. It makes one proxy at a time, 4:2:2 clips first, so it only takes longer when you keep playing.

q: What are the proxy mode settings?
a: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Media… ▸ Proxies: Auto (default: proxies while playing, the original when paused), Always use proxies, or Never use proxies (kept but unused, no new ones queued); command `media.proxyMode` with `auto`, `on` or `off`. Untick Create proxies automatically for 4K and larger long-GOP clips (`media.autoProxies`) to stop automatic creation; ticking it queues proxies for large clips already in the project.

q: In Resolve I'd switch Playback ▸ Use Proxy Media. What's the Revolution equivalent?
a: Settings ▸ Media ▸ Proxies (Auto, Always, Never), or the monitor's Toggle Proxies button for a quick Always / Never switch.

q: How do I make the automatic-style proxy for a clip it skipped?
a: Select the clips and run `media.createProxies` with `preset` `auto`: it goes to the background worker like the automatic ones. Clip ▸ Proxy ▸ Create Proxies… makes other presets (ProRes or H.264, quarter or half size) as a foreground job, and Attach Proxies… (`media.attachProxies`) attaches your own files, which Revolution never replaces.

q: How do I attach proxies I made elsewhere?
a: Select the clips and run `media.createProxies` with `preset` `auto`: it goes to the background worker like the automatic ones. Clip ▸ Proxy ▸ Create Proxies… makes other presets (ProRes or H.264, quarter or half size) as a foreground job, and Attach Proxies… (`media.attachProxies`) attaches your own files, which Revolution never replaces.

q: In Premiere I'd render effects In to Out to get a red bar green. Is that automatic here?
a: Yes: the render cache writes the same kind of files automatically while you're idle. Sequence ▸ Render Effects In to Out (`sequence.renderEffectsInToOut`) still works by hand, runs at once and fills the same bar.

q: Why is there no colour on the render bar over some clips?
a: No colour means the clip plays as it is: one ungraded clip without effects at the sequence's size and frame rate. Hover the bar to read what any stretch is.

q: Does a ripple edit invalidate the cache?
a: Cached files are named after everything that affects their pictures. Editing a clip turns its stretch yellow or red again; undo brings back the old files at once; relinking is a different picture, so it renders again; a ripple move keeps the files, since they're named relative to the stretch, not the timeline position; proxies don't count.

q: Does relinking a clip re-render its cache?
a: Cached files are named after everything that affects their pictures. Editing a clip turns its stretch yellow or red again; undo brings back the old files at once; relinking is a different picture, so it renders again; a ripple move keeps the files, since they're named relative to the stretch, not the timeline position; proxies don't count.

q: Why are cache pieces only 2 seconds long?
a: Each stretch between cuts is cached in 2-second pieces, each starting with a complete picture, so at a cut playback opens the next small file instead of decoding up to a second of camera footage, and the next piece is opened just before it's needed.

In Settings ▸ Media Cache ▸ Render Cache, Pause (`cache.pause`) stops the cache for this session and deletes the unfinished piece; it then reads Resume. Delete Unused (`cache.clearUnused`) deletes cache files no sequence of the project uses (such as undone versions), which then render again if needed. `cache.status` reports mode, pieces, size, limit and queue.

q: What happens to old preview files from earlier versions?
a: The first time a project is opened with this version, older preview files no sequence uses are deleted once. Unfinished files left by a crash (`….mov.part`) are deleted the next time the project opens. Each project only deletes files it made itself.

q: What are .mov.part files in the previews folder?
